_about: API catalog: every API this server uses or has evaluated, for any session or person with MCP access, so nobody re-researches an API already tried. Served by apis.list / apis.find. NEVER put secret values here: `auth` names the environment variable that holds a key. status: live = working now. An api_catalog.private.json next to this file adds entries, or replaces ones with the same name.

apis.name: Your own model (local)
apis.provider: any OpenAI-compatible server you run (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM)
apis.how_to_use: Set LOCAL_AI_BASE_URL and LOCAL_AI_MODEL (homeshed-mcp setup prints them for a running server); local_ai.ask model=auto tries it first
apis.notes: Free and private: prompts stay on your machine.

apis.name: NVIDIA hosted models (Nemotron)
apis.how_to_use: Set NVIDIA_API_KEY; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1. A free key for prototyping. Prompts leave your machine. Its reasoning models need enable_thinking=false, which local_ai.ask sends by default.

apis.name: Your own gateway (e.g. LiteLLM)
apis.how_to_use: Set LOCAL_AI_GATEWAY_URL and LOCAL_AI_GATEWAY_KEY; local_ai.ask uses its nvidia-* models as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: Only the gateway's nvidia-* models are used. Prompts leave your machine if the gateway sends them on.

apis.name: Groq
apis.how_to_use: Set GROQ_API_KEY; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://api.groq.com/openai/v1. About 100 requests a minute on the free tier. Prompts leave your machine.

apis.name: OpenRouter (free models)
apis.how_to_use: Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. Free models only (ids end in :free): 20 a minute, 50 a day. Prompts leave your machine.

apis.name: Mistral AI
apis.how_to_use: Set MISTRAL_API_KEY; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://api.mistral.ai/v1. About 1 request a second on the free tier. Prompts leave your machine.

apis.name: Google Gemini
apis.how_to_use: Set GEMINI_API_KEY; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai. About 15 a minute and 1,500 a day on the free Flash models. Prompts leave your machine.

apis.name: OVHcloud AI Endpoints
apis.how_to_use: Set OVH_AI_ENDPOINTS_TOKEN; local_ai.ask then uses it automatically as a cloud fallback
apis.notes: OpenAI-compatible at https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1. Anonymous use is 2 a minute; a free token raises it. Prompts leave your machine.

apis.name: Shared memory
apis.provider: the built-in store (SQLite), or a self-hosted TDAI memory-core
apis.auth: none for the built-in store; memory-core's keys in the environment
apis.notes: Cross-session facts and history, kept per project, for every client with MCP access.

apis.name: Push notifications (ntfy)
apis.provider: ntfy.sh, or your own ntfy server (NTFY_BASE_URL)
apis.notes: Your phone follows the topic in the ntfy app.

apis.name: Jina Reader
apis.notes: Webpage-to-markdown. SSRF-hardened URL validation before any request. Rate-limited without a key.

apis.name: Uptime Kuma
apis.provider: your Uptime Kuma (its database file, mounted read-only)
apis.notes: Monitor states; Uptime Kuma sends its own outage alerts.

apis.name: Docker engine
apis.provider: the Docker daemon on the server's host
apis.auth: the Docker socket, mounted only if you use these tools (it gives root on the host)

apis.name: Open-Meteo
apis.cost: free for non-commercial use only (<10,000 calls a day)
apis.notes: Terms checked 2026-09-29: "You may only use the free API services for non-commercial purposes." A paid plan is needed inside anything sold. Fine for the owner's own use.

apis.name: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap geocoding)
apis.cost: free, under a strict usage policy
apis.auth: none; an identifying User-Agent is required
apis.how_to_use: GET https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=..&format=json with a User-Agent naming the app
apis.notes: Policy checked 2026-09-29: at most 1 request a second, cache results, show OpenStreetMap attribution; no autocomplete, no bulk or grid jobs, no reselling. Self-host Nominatim for heavy use.

apis.name: Frankfurter (exchange rates)
apis.how_to_use: https://api.frankfurter.dev: latest and historical rates by base currency (see its docs for the current /v1 and /v2 paths)
apis.notes: Checked 2026-09-29: free, no key, commercial use allowed ("the rates themselves fall under each provider's terms"); rates from 104 central banks; rate-limited against abuse, no quotas. Cache results; it can be self-hosted.

apis.name: Wikipedia (Wikimedia REST)
apis.auth: none; User-Agent with contact details required
apis.notes: Checked 2026-09-29: no key; 200 requests a minute with a User-Agent naming the app plus a contact URL or email, only 10 a minute without. Content is CC BY-SA: credit Wikipedia when showing it.
